we’re hiring and training canvass directors to make an impact on some of the most important problems of our time — like protecting wildlife and wild places, eliminating plastic waste that is polluting our oceans, ensuring we have clean air to breathe and clean water to drink, and more. having policy solutions to these problems often isn’t enough to make the changes we need. to win positive change, we need to educate, engage and mobilize people across the country to support those solutions.we’re hiring canvass directors to build the people power it takes to tackle these problems and win. directors and their staff work to build public support through one-on-one, face-to-face conversations on america’s front doorsteps, generating the kind of support that lasts longer than a news cycle and goes deeper than an online petition. this position requires exercising discretion and independent judgment in making decisions in matters of significance. we have immediate positions available as well as positions starting throughout the year.apply to work with us if you want to:educate and engage the public on campaigns like protecting forests and the wildlife that depend on them, moving beyond single-use plastics and stopping electronic waste.build support and fundraise for leading nonprofit groups working on these issues, including environment america and pirg.hire, train and manage your own team.work at the most effective citizen outreach operation in the country. we have raised over $700 million for environmental and public interest organizations, run hundreds of campaigns in all 50 states, and educated and mobilized millions of people on important issues.qualificationswe are looking for candidates who have leadership experience and potential, excellent communication skills, and who want to work hard to make lasting, positive change on important issues. being a canvass director requires that you work independently, exercise good judgment and work hard to meet your office’s staffing, campaign and fieldwork goals.trainingwe have an excellent training program, which starts with working in an existing canvass office to get hands-on training, as well as classroom-style training on social change concepts and skills.throughout the year, new and experienced canvass directors may participate in advanced trainings on staff management, canvassing, campaign strategy and other skills.locationswe work on campaigns and in locations that we think will make the biggest difference. we are looking for canvass directors who are ready to go where they’re needed most and wherever they can make the biggest impact. canvass directors could work on campaigns almost anywhere in the country, and while location preferences are considered for placements, we require all directors to be geographically flexible. right now we are running campaigns in california, colorado, d.c., illinois, massachusetts, minnesota, north carolina, oregon, pennsylvania, washington state and wisconsin.pay and benefitsthe target annual compensation for this position is $40,000-$53,750, depending on position and location. the fund offers an excellent benefits package. our benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees and dependents, paid sick time (60-80 hours/year depending on location), vacation time (accruing 10 days over year 1, 15 days over year 2, and 20 days over year 3 and thereafter), a commuter benefit program, a 401(k) plan with employer match, parental leave, long term disability insurance, and may include needs-based student loan assistance. we also offer an excellent training program and opportunities for advancement.apply: apply online here.why work with us? check out 10 reasons: https://fundforthepublicinterest.org/canvass-directorabout fund for the public interestthe fund’s mission is to build public support to tackle some of america’s toughest problems. at a time when people spend so much of their lives facing screens, the fund's citizen outreach team builds public support face-to-face, person-to-person for important issues. and it works. for more than 40 years, we've won support for reducing plastic waste, saving endangered wildlife, keeping toxic pollution out of our air and water, and more.as part of the public interest network, we represent some of the nation's most effective advocacy groups, including pirg (public interest research group) and environment america. starting with our door-to-door canvass, and following up through the mail, by phone this position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. our partner is looking for a director of marketing & public affairs based in the united states.the director of marketing & public affairs will lead integrated marketing, strategic communications, media relations, and public affairs initiatives for a mission-driven organization focused on financial security and economic opportunity. this senior leadership role will strengthen organizational visibility, expand audience engagement, and position key research, policy insights, and expertise within public and media conversations. you will oversee digital strategy, executive communications, creative campaigns, and media outreach while translating organizational priorities into measurable results. working closely with senior leadership and cross-functional teams, you will ensure communications are timely, impactful, and aligned with broader organizational goals. the role combines strategic planning, team leadership, performance measurement, and external relationship management. this is an opportunity to shape public narratives, amplify meaningful work, and contribute to initiatives that advance economic stability and financial well-being.accountabilitiesmarketing & public affairs strategy: develop and lead an integrated marketing and public affairs strategy aligned with organizational, programmatic, policy, and revenue objectives. maintain forward-looking 30-, 60-, and 90-day plans, anticipate communications opportunities, and provide senior leadership with clear recommendations and actionable priorities.media relations & executive visibility: build relationships with national, regional, trade, and policy journalists; develop proactive media strategies; oversee press releases, statements, opinion pieces, and media pitches; and position executives and subject-matter experts as credible voices in relevant public discussions.executive communications: prepare senior leaders for media appearances, speeches, panels, and external engagements by coordinating briefing materials, research, supporting data, practitioner stories, and anticipated questions well in advance.digital marketing & audience growth: lead digital communications across social media, email, and web channels. establish audience growth and engagement objectives, manage editorial calendars, optimize platform-specific content, and expand the use of short-form video and other effective digital formats.campaign & creative management: plan major campaigns, announcements, reports, and events from inception through execution. develop creative briefs, coordinate copywriting, design, video, paid media, and executive participation, and ensure campaigns receive effective promotion and follow-up.team & vendor leadership: manage, coach, and develop marketing and public affairs staff. oversee consultants, creative agencies, and external vendors, establishing clear deliverables, budgets, deadlines, and performance expectations while evaluating internal versus external resource needs.cross-functional collaboration: partner with policy, research, programs, business development, finance, and senior leadership teams to align messaging, clarify responsibilities, and ensure communications requirements are identified, resourced, and scheduled appropriately.scope & resource management: evaluate grant-funded communications obligations, monitor team capacity, manage competing priorities, and raise potential risks early. recommend alternatives when requests exceed agreed scope, budgets, or available resources.revenue & partnership support: collaborate with business development teams to develop promotional assets, audience insights, case studies, and sponsorship opportunities. support fundraising, donor stewardship, partnership visibility, and the strategic use of organizational content and events.performance measurement & optimization: establish measurable performance indicators for audience growth, engagement, earned media, paid campaigns, registrations, lead generation, and partnership support. analyze results, recommend improvements, optimize advertising spend, and communicate the function's impact to senior leadership and the board.organizational leadership: promote clear communication, accountability, proactive problem-solving, and constructive collaboration in a remote environment. participate in organizational planning and performance processes while maintaining high standards of accuracy, responsiveness, and execution.requirementseducation: bachelor's degree in communications, marketing, public affairs, journalism, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.professional experience: approximately 7 or more years of progressively responsible experience in marketing, public affairs, media relations, strategic communications, or a related discipline.leadership & management: demonstrated experience managing employees, consultants, vendors, budgets, or complex cross-functional initiatives, with the ability to coach teams, delegate effectively, and oversee multiple priorities.strategic communications: proven success developing and executing communications or marketing strategies that improve organizational visibility, audience engagement, participation, or public influence.media relations: experience building journalist relationships, pitching stories, developing press materials, and preparing executives for interviews and public appearances.digital marketing expertise: strong understanding of social media strategy, digital engagement, audience development, editorial planning, campaign execution, and performance analytics.writing & content development: excellent writing, editing, and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex research, policy, and organizational priorities into clear, accessible messages for diverse audiences.analytical & strategic thinking: ability to interpret performance data, identify opportunities, test new approaches, make evidence-based recommendations, and communicate trade-offs effectively.resource & budget management: experience overseeing external vendors, evaluating resource allocation, managing spending, and ensuring communications initiatives deliver measurable value.stakeholder management: strong interpersonal and communication skills, with experience collaborating across departments and engaging senior executives, external partners, media representatives, and other stakeholders.technology: familiarity with crm platforms, digital engagement tools, and analytics systems. salesforce experience is an advantage.professional judgment: ability to challenge assumptions constructively, address emerging issues, anticipate organizational needs, and manage competing deadlines with accuracy and composure.industry background: experience in nonprofit organizations, government, financial services, economic policy, or another mission-driven environment is beneficial but not required.work arrangement & travel: ability to work remotely, collaborate regularly during eastern time core hours, and coordinate across time zones. travel of approximately 20%–25% is expected for organizational meetings, conferences, media engagements, partner activities, and other events.supervisory responsibility: this position requires direct management of staff and external consultants.benefitsannual salary: $112,849–$163,631, depending on qualifications and relevant experience.work arrangement: fully remote position, with regular collaboration during eastern time core hours.leadership opportunities: senior-level responsibility for shaping integrated marketing, public affairs, media strategy, and organizational communications.professional impact: opportunity to amplify research, policy expertise, and initiatives that advance financial security and economic opportunity.cross-functional exposure: collaboration with senior executives and teams across policy, research, programs, business development, and other organizational functions.professional development: opportunities to strengthen strategic leadership, team management, media relations, and digital communications expertise.travel & external engagement: approximately 20%–25% travel, the final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.we appreciate your interest and wish you the best! why apply through jobgether?data privacy notice: by verification signals in application materials based on available information. these tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. if you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
